newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Hyatt to break into Colombia tourism market.
newsitem.headline: Hyatt to break into Colombia tourism market.

text.p: U.S. hotel chain Hyatt International plans a $60 million complex on the Caribbean coast, one of the project heads said Tuesday.

"We carried out studies which showed that Cartagena needed a project of this size. Hyatt's participation has been achieved after years of negotiation," said Roberto Guerrero, chairman of investment company Promotora El Faro and head of development for the project.
Work on the 351-room hotel in the resort town of Cartagena, about 375 miles (600 km) north of Bogota, is expected to begin in the first half of 1997 and will take about two years to complete.
The Gran Hyatt project is backed by a consortium of international and Colombian investors. It will include a casino, golf course, convention center and sports facilities.

In the last three years the number of luxury hotels in Colombia has almost tripled. According to the Colombian Hotel Association, there are now 108 four and five-star establishments, with a total of almost 18,500 rooms, compared with just 34 such hotels in 1993, with less than 4,500 rooms.
